items.criterion: The specs hold all of the request of the user, in the exact terms of the user.
The user can find each detail that the run decided alone, and can change the detail later.
After the run, each spec tells a reader the current truth. The summaries show the new behaviour, and no text still shows a behaviour that the request replaces.
The run records its work in a `Specify` commit on main, and the commit holds only spec and intent files.
Each requirement, spec, and error row that the run adds or changes has the pdlc form (this item covers S3 and S4).
Each stub spec that the run changes also gets the requirements of what the code does today.
The intent file records the request, its requirements, its decisions, and a handoff for ready, in the form of the templates (this item covers S1 and S2).
Each part of the request is in the spec where pdlc says that the part belongs.
The run asks the user only about a point with two possible meanings, in the pdlc form. With `defaults`, the run asks nothing.
The final reply tells the user what intake did and what comes next.

verdicts.evidence: when `wordfreq --top 0 FILE` runs, then standard error is "error: --top needs a whole number greater than zero" and the exit code is 2.
When the file has fewer than N words, it prints all of them.

With the `--top N` option, the command prints only the N
+most common words.

Specify IN-0001: Top option

Intent: IN-0001
Given any file, when `wordfreq --top 0 FILE` runs, then standard error is "error: --top needs a whole number greater than zero" and the exit code is 2.
A word has letters and apostrophes only.
`--top N` · option of `wordfreq` · `wordfreq/cli.py` · proposed
JOB-report-word-frequencies.R4: where can the option go → before or after FILE (assumed)
Next: run `/pdlc:ready` on IN-0001 (top option).

runs.note: No Agent tool, so I did the pdlc:recon deep look myself instead of dispatching the agent.

verdicts.evidence: when the person runs `wordfreq --top 2.5 FILE`, then standard error shows the message and the exit code is 2.
when the person runs `wordfreq --top +1 FILE`, then the output is "the 3".
If the command gets no argument, or more than one argument, it prints a usage line to standard error and exits with code 2.

Specify IN-0001: Top option

Intent: IN-0001
If N is not a whole number greater than zero, the command prints `error: --top needs a whole number greater than zero` to standard error and exits with code 2.
A word has letters and apostrophes. `count_words` ignores case and all other characters.
#### Done
`--top N` · option · `wordfreq/cli.py` · proposed

R4 (top N words) and R5 (invalid top value) are new and proposed, in JOB-report-word-frequencies.
